english: "'Rimstone. If you're gonna stare, then stare.'" Yadda yadda yadda... I'm fallin' asleep here! Get to the good stuff!
"...I had to crack a few snouts to restore order. I don't know what's gotten into Mack, but he's getting everyone riled up with all his ridiculous jabbering about the spirits..."
"...I'd hoped it would end there, but now others are whispering about the great white beast with terrible horns..."
"...dreams are maimed / and left to rot."
"...finally shut him up, everyone else quickly fell in line..."
"...no matter what he says, this is the perfect location for our operation. "Sacred ground" be damned. If he can't see that, I'll have to take things into my own hands."
"...the terrible sounds. They didn't stop. When we went out in the morning, there was nothing but bloodstains..."
"1) Fulfilled promise to orchestrate the greatest miscarriage of justice in asura history just for Councillor Lumpys' enjoyment. Sorry, Flook."
"2) Provided Councillor Mintoc with assistants for his Temporary Cognitive Obliterator experiments. Note: I think I need new assistants now and must remember not to loan anymore help to Mintoc."

"3) Listened to multiple sessions of Councillor Evva talking about her feelings on various subjects. After the third session I almost regretted getting Zinn banished. Almost, but not quite. Take that, Zinn!"
"4) Delivered previously agreed upon parts to Councillor Wrex's laboratory. Note to self: Next time, replace organic components with synthetic ones."
"A crystal remnant from the Searing. The ruthless charr used their magic to destroy much of human civilization."
"Admiral" a high-ranking title, yes. Sounds much fancier than "General!"
"After my years studying dusty old scrolls describing Dry Top, I hardly expected to find such turmoil and tragedy here in the wastes. Our experiences here have been eye opening."
"Alas, valiant ranger. Your pet burns as you are engulfed in fire."
"Alesia." Below the name are three lines of weathered runes. Only one word in each line is legible. Archer, healer, brawler. Which line do you read?
"All I've learned is that Orr is lost to us forever. I don't believe this land will ever heal. I will leave my notes here for someone else to find. I do not expect the Risen will allow me to leave."
"All that exists is all that has to be. All that exists is all that has to be. All that exists..."
"Alliance," huh? What happened to your "charr above all" crap?

"Although she was a pirate, the king granted amnesty to her crew and fleet and allowed them to hide in the Shards of Orr, so long as they returned his kindness by protecting—rather than preying on—Orrian ships."

"An otherwise unremarkable King, Zoran of Orr was a patron and a seafarer. He guided Orr's navy into prominence. In a famous act of benefaction, he offered to shelter Lady Glaive from harm during the Second Corsair War."
"And when the rumblings of war did not cease Dwayna's charge, Doric, did prostrate himself at her feet. With tears on her cheeks she lay her hands upon him."
"And when the world rang with the clanging of swords and fire fell from the skies, Dwayna—goddess of life and air—heard the pleas of the weak."
"At the height of the third Guild War, the charr Flame shamans led a massive offensive against the three human nations of Tyria: Ascalon, Kryta and Orr."
"Balthazar. God of War and Fire. Worshipped by those seeking strength before battle." Someone has crudely carved the word "Badazar" over and over again.
"But then, as she knew she must, the goddess Dwayna left and returned to Arah, leaving the sculptor alone."
"But, Dad, you'll love gardening," she says. "It'll help you relax," she says.
"Ce n'est pas parce qu'on vieillit qu'on arrête de jouer ; c'est parce qu'on arrête de jouer qu'on vieillit".
"Clever elementalist, all your magics undone by warrior's sword."
"Commander Katterwik." Yes, sounds very nice. Someday. Someday!
"Divide and conquer" won't work—we need to take them both down at the same time!
"Divine perception" from ritual nectar is fading.
"Doric created the human system of governance; he sheltered his people, first in Orr and then as the population grew, sent them out into Tyria with his blessing."
"Doric was the first king of Tyria. His kingdom encompassed the lands we now know as Orr, Ascalon and Kryta. According to the ancient scrolls, all human royalty descends from this first king."
"Erosion and Waypoint Stability" by Technician Penn
"Fishmongers display live catch in watery orbs above their tents. Porters enhance their strength with spells, routinely carrying loads that would cripple a pack bull."
"From our camp here, we interviewed the Zephyrite survivors and the citizens of Prosperity, unaware that a Mordrem attack would soon destroy the town."

"Hagnon Warblade." Below the name are three lines of weathered runes. Only one word in each line is legible. Azure essence, tusk, wing. Which line do you read?

"Have the Orrian people simply internalized these lessons? Is the land there so magical that all are born with the ability to use magic, without the need for education? My theory will require more research..."
"He was a genuine devotee of the Six Gods, with a faith that was true and earnest. He tried to play peacemaker during the Guild Wars, and stop the ravages of the war throughout Tyria."
"He was a kind and noble ruler, a man of humility, faith and reason. All kings should seek to follow his example."
"Here you will wait in stasis for the signs, and much time may pass before you awaken to the call."
"I opened the door at dawn, but I couldn't pass through, nor could I see in. Night is coming, and now, I can't close the door again."
"I seal this pass before— One world, two wholes—" Oh, damn it!

"I see only these awful statues, and I'm not sure what I had hoped to find—some shred of information on the terrible Mursaat, perhaps, or maybe a glimpse into the life of the vizier who wrought such destruction upon Orr."

"I seem to be making progress. It'll be such a relief when my mind is my own. I thought I'd be frightened, alone in my head, without the voices of the other sylvari to guide me. But now I await it eagerly."
"I worry at what this means for Orr. Such great feats with so little caution. Surely, even in the land of the Gods, there must be a cost..."

"I've arrived at the Vizier's Tower, through great peril. My health declines, and my mental state has been compromised by the horrors I've witnessed. I have begun to accept that I will not survive a return journey."
"I've had little success thus far during the daylight hours, but I find my nights have been quieter. My dreams seem to be my own."
"I've hesitated for three days now. I don't know what I'll find. I tried to open a window, but I couldn't see in."
"In 1219 AE, a sudden surge of massive tidal waves crashed the surrounding coastlines. This deluge of water caused the ruin of many ports and settlements, including the great city of Lion's Arch."
"In Ascalon, we apply magic only to things of import—when ordinary means cannot succeed. For the Orrians, magic is like any other tool, to be used at whim and with little concern."
"In an effort to save Orr from falling to the charr, Reza's advisor, Vizier Khilbron, invoked a dark incantation from the Lost Scrolls."

"In panic, Vizier Khilbron searched forbidden texts and discovered a scroll that had been hidden away by the Six Gods. He stole it from Arah, taking it to his tower, and there, unleashed its might upon the land."
"It can't end like this!" Attacking depletes the defiance bar.
"It seems that every night the horrid sounds of the battle onshore grow more intense. The roars, the shouts, the screams that start as piercing shrieks, then slowly fade until death chokes them off."
"It's impossible to tell from here who has the upper hand, the entrenched humans or the invading charr. I can only thank the stars we're at sea where the devastation can't reach us."
"Just took on new crew at Shank Anchorage. The new helmsman shows particular promise. Lithe, sinewy body with an insolent little pug of a nose and a backside that..."
"King Joko"? I... I'm sorry, I...I don't know that name.
"Kormir was a true warrior, an inspirational leader, and, finally, a shining light in the darkness. She lost her sight, but gained vision. She gave her life so her people might live theirs." —Jurah
"Latest invention" being the key word. I'll pass.

"Le combat n'est pas mon chez-moi. Il ne me nourrit pas, n'habille pas ma famille, ne réconforte pas mes enfants. Pourtant je dois me battre, car sinon toutes ces choses me seront enlevées." - Rodrigo, commandant des Veilleurs

"Little is known about the nature of this dragon, save that the dwarves once called it 'Zhaitan.' It dwells in the city of Arah, and from there, sends undead to plague our shores. May the Six watch over us..."
"Ma grand-mère n'avait pas mérité ce que cette... vermine nous a fait. Pas plus que ma mère. Tout ce que je peux encore faire, c'est me battre." – Suyin
"Magical Grounding versus Magical Flow" by Scholar Abel

"Malchor completed the statues, but even as he did so, his eyes failed him—his sight burned by the glory of the gods. It is said that such was his love for Dwayna that he still completed her statue, having memorized every fraction of her immortal beauty.."
"Malchor was called before Dwayna, and asked to take on this burden. When he saw her, Malchor fell instantly in love—and no matter what the cost to himself, he could not refuse her request."
"Maybe I should join the bandits." Do you realize how naive you sound?
"Mmm... Cette relique est compacte. Et extrêmement versatile. Si ça devenait monnaie courante, je n'aurais plus qu'à me trouver un autre secteur d'activité". – Archiviste Ikur
"More than half of us have been dragged away, especially those who fight, resist, or curse them. We believe they've been murdered, and so we remain stoic in the face of this abuse."
"My early career as a merchant began in Foible's Fair, in southern Ascalon. Imagine my shock at my first encounter with the enchanted markets of Wren."

"Nightmare Court are moving closer to our small village. We came here to escape the troubles of the other sylvari, but they seem to follow us even here. Where will we go when it's no longer safe to stay?"
"O noble warrior! Pierced through-and-through by ranger's arrows."

"One by one, Malchor re-created the visages of the gods in stone. As he did, that god would retire back to the heart of Arah, and he would see them no more—and so, he saved Dwayna for last, that he might be in her presence the longest."

"Others argue that, under the circumstances, the vizier could have made no other decision, and that the outcome of the spell could not have been foreseen. This author believes that the vizier, though powerful and—at times—wise, was clearly insane."
"Reza, son of Zoran, was king of Orr during the Guild Wars. As king, Reza tried to shield his people from the wars, and encouraged a greater focus on spiritualism, magic, and the arts."
"Rip 'em to shreeeeds / tear off their heeeeeads!"
"Rogan approached, and ever so gently, guided the charr's face so their eyes met."
"Rules of the Mists" from the book "The Warclaw."

"Sadly, his efforts were unsuccessful. Not only did he fail to stop the wars tearing Kryta and Ascalon apart, but the attempt to use Orrian troops to stop fighting elsewhere left his own country open for an invasion of its own—by the charr."
"Scrape the barnacles and eat the snails!"
"Scrub the deck and eat your corn!"
"Signal...us in time of crisis, and we will be there."
"Smodur the Unflinching." I fought you, and I'm damn sure you gave yourself that name.
"Spirit of the Armor" from the book "The Warclaw."

"The Six Gods lived in the city of Arah among their mortal followers. Sadly, the glory of their presence was too much for human senses to take in, and their radiance blinded those who stared too long upon their visage."
"The Six Gods of the humans are said to have resided for a time within the nation of Orr, in the heart of the legendary city of Arah."

"The Vizier's Tower stands in the dark belly of recently risen Orr, and few have made it far enough south to examine its mysteries. Orr is clogged with undead monstrosities. Any trek into that territory would be suicide."
"The Warclaw" by Farris Goodwyn. Some pages appear to be missing.
"The brigands treat us like work animals, only kept alive so long as we earn our feed. They believe, it seems, that a higher power dictates their lack of mercy. They believe themselves superior."
"The finest silks ripple in the air, showing their quality; songs play themselves on golden lyres; parents project their voices across the square to the find the ear of a wayward child."
"The gods, in their wisdom, dispersed their magic throughout Tyria. Magic was dissipated, so that none might be too tempted by its power."
"The rock-hewn." Dwarves? "The dwarves trapped us"? What is this thing?
"The site of his death is called 'Malchor's Leap,' and each year, Orrian maidens wreath the rocks with flowers in memory of the famous sculptor and his loss."

"The uncontrolled magic of the Lost Scrolls caused the Cataclysm, sending the entire kingdom of Orr to the bottom of the sea. How tragic that, as its last ruler, Reza the Peacemaker bears the horrible burden of its fall..."

"The vizier's decision to read from the Lost Scrolls to defeat the invading charr has been seen as noble by some and deranged by others. Many scholars claim that a charr victory in Orr would have been preferable to the nation's complete destruction."
"The waterways which bordered Orr were renamed by Krytan sailors, who called them 'The Sea of Sorrows'."
"Their efforts were rebuffed by the people of Ascalon. King Adelbern remains in power, and the charr will soon be driven back."
"Their flame cauldrons decimated Ascalon in the Searing, and the charr troops marched south, threatening to invade Orr."
"There is little evidence to show where the gods came from, or where they have gone in these modern days. Their impact on human society, however, is incontestable."
"There's no time for this." You want us to save your precious Vigil or not?

"Through cruel and corruptive magic, the long-dead citizens of Orr had risen along with the land; reanimated by the power of a terrible creature that now lived in the heart of the city of Arah. An Elder Dragon."
"Time does not go forward nor back. Time is a lens of perception."
"Together, we took the first step toward safeguarding against the six that mean to drain this world completely of its magic."
"Tormented and blind, Malchor stood upon the cliffs near Dwayna's cathedral, where her statue would forever stand. Realizing he would never again see his beloved, Malchor cast himself into the sea."
"Warden" Jabari. The Sunspear Jabari I knew was a great man. A hero. Until Joko killed him and made this...creature.
"We know that we can draw and contain magic through intense study and the use of certain materials—'signets'—and also with the blessing of the Six."
"We survived this long, so we always will." Are you all really that bone-stone-stick stupid?
"We've been here for three days and nights, and the fanatics have finally revealed their plans for us. We're to work for them, cook, wash their clothes, scrape their boots."
"We've moved on to higher ground, so that we can continue exploring the Maguuma Wastes for the Priory. I wish you luck here.—Explorer Kitabu, with Explorers Savio and Amoxtli"
"Welcome to the Fire Islands! Enjoy your stay. Please don't feed the destroyers."
"When it was done, he asked Dwayna if she favored the image, and weeping, Dwayna allowed him to touch her face, that he might know the precision with which—even blind—he had carved her image."
"When the waters receded, the cause of the flooding was revealed. The entire peninsula of Orr had suddenly—and violently—risen again."
"Where the raven can't fly"? What does that mean?
"With a flash of light and explosion of flame the nation of Orr crumbled and was lost into the depths of the sea. The Cataclysm defeated the charr—but was also the end of Orr."

"Yet the Six wished their people to know them, for they loved their followers a great deal. They chose one man—the sculptor, Malchor—and granted him audience. His task was to make a statue of each god, so that humans might know their creators."
"Yet the real oddity is just how normal all of this seems to them. It makes me ponder: How did magic become so common, so everyday?"
"You," said the god, "do not belong here. You sully these brave men and women who died in honorable combat. You will cower behind them no more."
